items.heading: Descaling an electric kettle
precautionsFirst: Unplug the kettle before cleaning, and let it cool if recently used.
details: Fill the kettle halfway with equal parts water and white vinegar, or a tablespoon of citric acid in water.
Let it sit for 20-30 minutes, or boil once and let it stand.
Scrub the interior gently with a soft brush or sponge, avoiding the heating element if exposed.
Rinse thoroughly several times with clean water before using it again.

items.heading: Cleaning a washing machine drum and dispenser
precautionsFirst: Run cleaning cycles empty, without any clothes inside.
details: Run an empty hot wash cycle with a cup of white vinegar or a washing-machine cleaner tablet.
Remove the detergent dispenser tray and soak it in warm soapy water, scrubbing off residue.
Wipe the rubber door seal on front-load machines thoroughly, as mold often builds up there.
Leave the door open after washes to let the drum air out and prevent musty smells.

items.heading: Cleaning an exhaust fan or chimney filter
precautionsFirst: Switch off and unplug the appliance before removing any parts.
details: Remove the filter mesh or grease filter, following the manual.
Soak it in hot water with dish soap or a degreaser for 20-30 minutes to loosen grease.
Scrub with a brush, rinse thoroughly, and dry completely before refitting.
Wipe down the fan blades and housing with a degreaser cloth.

items.heading: Removing common stains from clothes
precautionsFirst: Test any stain remover on a hidden part of the fabric first.
Treat stains as soon as possible, and avoid hot water or the dryer before treating, which can heat-set the stain.
details: For oil or grease: sprinkle talcum powder or cornstarch on the fresh stain to absorb the oil, brush it off, then work dish soap into the fabric before laundering.
For ink: dab, do not rub, with rubbing alcohol or hand sanitizer on a cotton ball from the back of the fabric, then wash.
For blood: rinse immediately in cold water, never hot, then soak in cold water with a little salt, or use hydrogen peroxide on white fabrics before washing.
For turmeric: rub with a paste of dish soap and baking soda, and leave in direct sunlight for a few hours before washing.
For wine or fruit juice: blot excess, sprinkle salt over the fresh stain, then rinse with cold water and wash as usual.

items.heading: Removing mold from bathroom tiles and grout
precautionsFirst: Ventilate the bathroom well and wear gloves - never mix bleach with other cleaning chemicals.
details: Make a paste of baking soda and water, or a mix of one part bleach to three parts water for tougher mold on white grout and tiles only.
Apply to the moldy area and let it sit for 10-15 minutes.
Scrub with an old toothbrush, focusing on the grout lines.
Rinse thoroughly and dry the area, and improve ventilation to prevent it recurring.

items.heading: Cleaning a clogged showerhead
precautionsFirst: Handle the showerhead gently to avoid scratching its finish.
details: Unscrew the showerhead, or leave it attached if it can be bagged in place.
Soak it in a bowl, or a plastic bag tied around it, of white vinegar for 30-60 minutes.
Scrub the nozzle holes with an old toothbrush or toothpick to clear mineral deposits.
Rinse thoroughly and reattach.

items.heading: Removing hard water stains from taps and sinks
precautionsFirst: Avoid abrasive scrubbers on shiny chrome fittings, which can scratch the surface.
details: Soak a cloth or paper towel in white vinegar and wrap it around the affected area for 15-30 minutes.
Scrub gently with a soft cloth or old toothbrush.
Rinse and dry with a soft towel to prevent new water spots.

items.heading: Cleaning burnt or blackened utensils
precautionsFirst: Let very hot pans cool before adding water, to avoid warping.
details: Sprinkle baking soda generously on the burnt area and add a little water to form a paste.
Let it sit for 15-30 minutes, or bring it to a gentle boil in the pan if the burn is stubborn.
Scrub with a scrubber or steel wool once cooled.
For non-stick pans, avoid steel wool - use a soft scrubber with the baking soda paste instead.

items.heading: Deodorizing smelly shoes
precautionsFirst: Ensure any powder used is fully shaken out before wearing the shoes again.
details: Sprinkle baking soda inside the shoes and leave overnight, then shake out before wearing.
Place a used dryer sheet, or a small cloth pouch of coffee grounds, inside the shoes when not in use.
Let shoes air out and dry fully between uses rather than storing them damp.

items.heading: Cleaning and maintaining wooden furniture
precautionsFirst: Avoid excess water on wood surfaces, which can cause warping or white marks.
details: Dust regularly with a soft, dry microfiber cloth.
For grime, wipe with a barely damp cloth and dry immediately with a separate cloth.
Apply a small amount of furniture polish, or a mix of olive oil and vinegar, occasionally to restore shine.
Use coasters and mats to prevent water rings and heat marks.

items.heading: Basic pest control for ants, cockroaches, and mosquitoes
precautionsFirst: Keep any pest control substances away from children and pets, and away from food preparation areas.
details: For ants: sprinkle a line of chalk, cinnamon, or a vinegar-water spray along entry points, and keep counters free of food residue.
For cockroaches: place a mix of boric acid, sugar, and flour in bottle caps in corners away from children and pets, and seal cracks and gaps.
For mosquitoes: remove standing water indoors and around the home weekly, fit mesh screens on windows, and consider a citronella or neem oil spray.
For persistent infestations, consider a professional pest control service.
